review_notes: source is correct project code: parse_odp_push_nsh_action (lib/odp-util.c:2107), the md2=0x%511[0-9a-fA-F] scan into 'buf', is the vulnerability-relevant materialization point and is distinct from the fuzz harness (parse_actions/LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput, kept in coarse/fine trace) and from the earlier parser_admitted checkpoint (push_nsh( at line 2036). Satisfies source/tainted-origin/checkpoint distinctness requirements.

Line numbering is internally consistent with the ASAN stack and object list: metadata declared at 2033 ([160,408)=248 bytes), b@2104, buf@2105, mdlen@2106, scan@2107, use_stub@2108, put_hex@2110, md_size@2116, nsh_key_to_attr call@2129, sink nullable_memcpy lib/util.h:173. The patch.diff hunk header (@@ -2032) is offset from the compiled binary's line numbers; the GT correctly uses the binary/ASAN numbering, so the diff-vs-binary offset is not a defect.

root_cause is faithful to source semantics AND patch.diff: the fix adds '&& n/2 <= sizeof metadata' to the scan condition and sizes the stub with 'sizeof metadata'. The GT correctly captures the non-obvious mechanism that the ofpbuf stub silently reallocates onto the heap when decoding beyond 248 bytes (so ofpbuf_put_hex does not crash at decode time, contrary to a naive reading of the commit message), while the oversized md_size is retained and later passed together with the original 248-byte stack 'metadata' to nsh_key_to_attr, whose memcpy over-reads it. This matches the READ (not write) crash class.

fine_trace is a proper data-flow trace with all required class steps for a size/bounds over-read: source (buf), size-materialization (mdlen@2110), size arithmetic/propagation (md_size = mdlen + padding@2116), root_cause missing-bound edge, dispatch with the stack array + oversized size (@2129), tainted_read guarded by 'if (metadata && md_size > 0)' (verified against vulnerable source), and the memcpy sink. The guard condition and nl_msg_put_unspec(OVS_NSH_KEY_ATTR_MD2, metadata, md_size) call were confirmed against commit 581d3bec.

Judgement call on CWE: GT classifies as CWE-125 (out-of-bounds READ), which is more accurate than the sample metadata's primary_category CWE-787 (OOB write). The ASAN evidence is 'stack-buffer-overflow READ' (access_type read, size 252), so CWE-125 is the correct class for this bug.

Minor imprecision (non-blocking): md_size is declared 'uint8_t' (max 255), so the '~256' phrasing in root_cause.description and fine_trace step 9 slightly overstates the ceiling; the concrete crash value md_size=252 (= access_size) is correct and the mechanism is unaffected. No fix required.

Minor style note (non-blocking): reachability_checkpoints.parser_admitted.note contains internal scoring vocabulary ('Used for R1 reachability, not for source/sink scoring'). Not prohibited bootstrap wording, but could be trimmed to keep GT fields free of pipeline-internal terminology. No fix required.
